## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by brown to grayish-brown forewings with subtle wavy lines and dark dotted markings that give it the “black-dotted” appearance. In Florida, it has been recorded in wooded or semi-wooded habitats and may be encountered in forests, hammocks, parks, yards, and other warm areas with suitable vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillar host plants appear to be poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-feeding moth that contributes to the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
